title: Managing Workflow Malleability in Urgent Computing for Earthquake Alerts
problem: Earthquake impact simulations must incorporate new seismic data during execution to provide accurate and timely information, but traditional rigid workflows cannot adapt without restart.
motivation: First responders need fast and accurate earthquake impact information to coordinate effective rescue and relief operations.
method: The UCIS4EQ platform uses PyCOMPSs to implement a malleable workflow that monitors for seismic data updates at runtime and dynamically incorporates them into ongoing 3D parallel simulations. The system manages multiple HPC jobs to execute the adaptive workflow while maintaining computational efficiency and result consistency.
key_novelty: Dynamic workflow malleability that enables real-time data integration during urgent computing execution, reducing computational resource consumption by 40% without sacrificing time-to-solution.
contributions: PyCOMPSs-based implementation of UCIS4EQ with runtime malleability support
Runtime data update mechanism that dynamically incorporates seismic information without workflow restart
40% reduction in computational resource usage while maintaining execution time
Reduced result variability through dynamic data integration
limitations: Validation limited to single earthquake dataset (Samos Izmir); broader scalability and generalization not discussed.
primary_theme: dynamic workflow adaptation for urgent seismic hazard assessment
